project.name: RefundLedger demonstration
project.description: Fictional local authorization ledger; no money movement, payment provider or deployment integration.

environments.title: One reservation attempt observed before and after

data.description: Prevent local refund authorizations from consuming more than the captured amount.
data.success_measure: Every accepted transition preserves CON-001; concurrency tests include atomic reservation.

data.description: Only an authenticated principal for the tenant may operate on that tenant ledger.
data.success_measure: Cross-tenant requests are denied and create no state change.

data.definition: A non-negative integer number of EUR cents. This example has one currency per payment and no conversion.
The immutable captured amount for one tenant/payment pair. This is a local authorization ceiling, not a payment-provider balance.
A refund record in reserved or committed state; released and rejected records do not consume capacity.
The tuple tenant_id, payment_id, key. Records are retained for the lifetime of this demonstration ledger.
A principal established outside request payloads by a trusted authentication adapter. Test fixtures simulate this adapter.

data.trigger: a reservation would consume more than the captured capacity
data.subject: RefundLedger
data.response: reject the reservation without changing the ledger

data.trigger: a request repeats an existing tenant/payment/key with the same payload
data.subject: RefundLedger
data.response: return the existing reservation identifier without adding a record

data.trigger: a tenant/payment/key is reused with a different payload
data.subject: RefundLedger
data.response: reject the conflicting request without changing the original record

data.trigger: the principal is unverified or the principal, request and target ledger tenants do not all match
data.subject: RefundLedger
data.response: deny the request without disclosing or changing another tenant ledger

data.trigger: a reserved authorization is definitively cancelled before commitment
data.subject: RefundLedger
data.response: release its capacity while retaining its idempotency record

data.trigger: an authorized commit command targets a reserved record
data.subject: RefundLedger
data.response: mark that record committed atomically without consuming capacity a second time

data.trigger: an authorization attempt completes or is denied
data.subject: RefundLedger
data.response: record the operation identifier and outcome without copying credentials or complete request bodies

data.responsibility: Reserve, release and commit records atomically.
Resolve verified tenant identity before ledger access.
data.boundary: Authentication data is not accepted from request parameters.
Audit persistence must not mutate the business outcome on replay.

data.threat: Two requests act on the same stale remaining amount.
data.impact: Accepted commitments exceed the declared captured capacity.

nodes.title: Authenticated caller and request agree but target ledger belongs to another tenant

data.expected: Deny access before disclosure or mutation because the target ledger is outside the authenticated tenant.

nodes.title: Keep diagnostics free of sensitive data

data.description: Audit and diagnostic output identifies an operation and its outcome without exposing credentials or complete request bodies.
data.success_measure: Inspection of emitted audit events finds no credential and no complete request payload.

data.description: A refund request from the ledger's tenant that fits the remaining captured amount is authorized.
data.success_measure: Fitting requests are reserved; the transition scenarios include admitted cases as well as refusals.

data.trigger: an authorized reservation request with an unused key fits the remaining captured capacity
data.subject: RefundLedger
data.response: record exactly one reserved authorization for the requested amount

nodes.title: Record left by a refused reservation

data.question: Does a refused reservation leave a rejected record in the ledger?
options: No record: the ledger is unchanged
A rejected record that consumes no capacity
data.answer: No record: the ledger is unchanged
data.rationale: REQ-001 already requires an unchanged ledger. The rejected status in the environments and MODEL-001 is then not written by this path; whether to remove it stays visible. This is a fictional reference decision.

nodes.title: An attempt that admits nothing leaves the ledger unchanged
An admitted reservation adds exactly one reserved record
Over-capacity request is refused and nothing changes

data.expected: The refusal leaves both existing records and the captured amount as they were.

nodes.title: Refusal that still wrote a record

data.expected: Detect the extra record: DEC-002 says a refusal leaves no record.

nodes.title: Identical retry returns the existing reservation

data.expected: The retry, including one sent after a lost response, adds no record.

nodes.title: Retry that created a second record

data.expected: Detect the duplicate: a replay must not add a record.

nodes.title: Conflicting reuse is refused and the original is intact

data.expected: The original record keeps its amount and status.

nodes.title: A new key is admitted beside an existing one

data.expected: Exactly one reserved record is added for the requested amount; the existing record is intact.
Detect that the recorded amount differs from the requested amount.
The denial leaves the ledger as it was.
